title: Carrier Onboarding Exception Report
subtitle: Carrier Onboarding: preserves facts, evidence, and actions.
description: Carrier Onboarding Exception Report covers carrier organization, operating authority, insurance, contacts, equipment, controls, and approval. The carrier onboarding coordinator records Carrier Onboarding chronology, evidence, containment, and effectiveness. Carrier Onboarding Exception Report keeps Carrier Onboarding exceptions visible until the carrier onboarding coordinator handoff.
use_case: Use Carrier Onboarding Exception Report at carrier file, qualification system, dispatch access, and document repository. Document carrier organization, operating authority, insurance, contacts, equipment, controls, and approval identity before Carrier Onboarding begins. Compare carrier organization, operating authority, insurance, contacts, equipment, controls, and approval findings with stated Carrier Onboarding criteria; route unresolved Carrier Onboarding issues to authorized carrier-compliance reviewer. For Carrier Onboarding Exception Report, confirm requirements for Carrier Onboarding. Ask authorized carrier-compliance reviewer to review Carrier Onboarding conditions beyond the carrier onboarding coordinator's role.

sections.title: Carrier Onboarding incident details
sections.guidance: Record when the issue was discovered, who reported it, the exact affected subject, and the initial condition.

blocks.label: Carrier Onboarding identity

fields.label: Authority, tax, insurance, and vendor identifiers
Dispatch, safety, claims, billing, and after-hours contacts

blocks.guidance: Use the Carrier Onboarding identifier printed on carrier organization, operating authority, insurance, contacts, equipment, controls, and approval or its linked source record.

blocks.label: Initial factual account, affected scope, and immediate containment

fields.label: Initial factual account, affected scope, and immediate containment

blocks.guidance: Separate direct observation from reported information, assumption, and unknown fact.

sections.title: Chronology, custody, and response
sections.guidance: Enter events in time order and identify the source of each fact and the person responsible for the response.

columns.label: Observed fact, event, or custody change

blocks.label: Unknown times, conflicting accounts, missing custody events, and source limitations

sections.title: Affected scope, evidence, and escalation
sections.guidance: Preserve volatile evidence, distinguish affected from unaffected scope, and keep required notifications visible.

blocks.label: Do not proceed without control
blocks.guidance: Stop normal processing when carrier identity, authority, insurance, fraud control, or authorized approval remains unresolved. Protect carrier organization, operating authority, insurance, contacts, equipment, controls, and approval; document the Carrier Onboarding notification and await authorized carrier-compliance reviewer direction.

blocks.label: Evidence preserved or linked
blocks.guidance: Attach or link proof for carrier organization, operating authority, insurance, contacts, equipment, controls, and approval; mark only Carrier Onboarding evidence present in that record.

blocks.label: Carrier Onboarding investigation points
items: Insurance type, limit, term, and source
Safety, security, tracking, and cargo controls
Payment, fraud, identity, and communication verification
Approval scope, conditions, expiration, and re-review
blocks.guidance: Record what was checked without converting an allegation, inference, or unavailable fact into an observation.

blocks.label: Severity, notification, and escalation triggers
items: Identity or ownership cannot be verified
blocks.guidance: For Carrier Onboarding, identify affected carrier organization, operating authority, insurance, contacts, equipment, controls, and approval scope; ask carrier onboarding coordinator to document the Carrier Onboarding immediate control before continuing.

sections.title: Corrective action, disposition, and review
sections.guidance: Track containment through disposition and an effectiveness check; do not close an incident merely because the immediate event stopped.
